game: Week 4 ATL@NO / kickoff MISSING / spread NOT saved / total NOT saved / weather not saved

script.base: Spread and total were not saved, so this script is inferred from team form only, not from a market number. ATL's run game is the stable unit (Bijan Robinson 66 carries, 349 yards, 5.29 YPC; Brian Robinson 30/132) against NO's soft run defense (4.85 YPC, 11 runs of 10+), so the base flow is ATL leaning on Bijan to stay on schedule and control pace. NO cannot lean on the run against ATL (3.12 YPC allowed, only 2 runs of 10+; Kamara 18/51 at 2.83 YPC, Etienne 31/128), so NO's path is the pass game, led by Olave (36 targets, 375 yards, 472 air yards), with Shough better when not blitzed (+0.11 EPA, n=47) and ATL blitzing only 21%. Competitive, ATL run-lean, NO pass-lean; not a shootout, because the ATL QB is -0.55 EPA/dropback when not blitzed and NO blitzes just 29%.
script.flip1: ATL's run game gets them ahead and they grind the clock; NO dropbacks shrink and Olave, Vele and Juwan Johnson yards stall even though NO cannot run.
script.flip2: ATL's no-blitz passing woes (-0.55 EPA) plus the 12 passes of 20+ yards ATL has already allowed put ATL in a hole; ATL abandons the run, Bijan's rush line dies, and NO's WR volume clears.

matchup.overlap: Bijan Robinson's 22.0 carries per game and 5.29 YPC attack the exact spot NO gives up (4.85 YPC, 11 explosive runs). Olave's 12.0 targets per game and 13.1 air yards per target attack ATL's explosive-pass leak (12 plays of 20+), and ATL's 21% blitz rate sits in Shough's better no-blitz split (+0.11 EPA).

market_rung_price: bijanrobinson rushyds over 87.5 at -114; chrisolave recyds over 86.5 at -116. Main lines only; no alt rungs and no no-vig in the pack. Short prices, used as the two correlated anchors of one script, not as plus-money alts.
pre_mortem: It's Monday and both lost because the unpriced spread was a NO lead the form read missed. ATL's -0.55 EPA when not blitzed never moved the ball, NO hit a couple of the explosive passes ATL has been allowing (12 of 20+ already), and Bijan was taken off the 22-carry pace toward 15 carries while Brian Robinson's 10-carry L3 role and a few stuffed runs left him at 70-80 rush yards, under 87.5. On the other leg, the clock-grind flip went the other way only after ATL's outside pass defense (5.86 YPA left, 5.63 right) took away Olave's 13.1 air-yards-per-target shots, his 30.5% share of 118 L3 targets produced 7 looks, and 125 yards of prior efficiency regressed into the 60s. That counter is real and is why Olave is a lean and both legs are script-tagged, but it is not stronger than the read: each line sits about 29-39 yards under the L3 average and the matchup points the same way as the role.
slip_story: One competitive split-script, the favorite-runs / opponent-throws shape without a saved spread: ATL runs because NO allows 4.85 YPC and 11 explosive runs (Bijan rush over), and NO throws because ATL allows 3.12 YPC and only 2 explosive runs while blitzing 21% (Olave rec over). They win together if the game stays competitive; they split in a blowout, so neither is a grind-only or shootout-only add-on. Do not add London or Pitts overs, a total under, or NO rush overs (Kamara 35.5, Miller 27.5, Shough 16.5); those need the other script or an injury the pack does not document. Two legs, no TDs, one market per player.
